title: Message queue: drop it off, do it later
intro: A food app takes orders faster than the kitchen cooks them. A queue sits in the middle to absorb the rush.

predict.question: The consumer crashes after receiving order 2 but before acknowledging it. What does the queue do?
options: Redeliver it, because it was never acknowledged
Delete it to keep the queue clean
predict.reveal: The queue only removes a message after an acknowledgement. No ack means it is delivered again, so nothing is lost.

takeaway: A queue decouples fast producers from slow consumers, buffers the rush, and redelivers until a consumer acknowledges.

steps.say: The order app (producer) and the kitchen worker (consumer) never talk directly. The queue sits between them.
A customer places order 1. The producer hands it to the queue and moves on at once.
The queue delivers order 1 to the idle consumer. It stays in the queue as 'in flight' until acknowledged.
A rush: order 2 arrives while the kitchen is busy. The producer does not wait; the queue holds it.
Order 3 arrives too. The slow consumer causes a backlog, but no order is dropped and the app stays fast.
Order 1 is done. The consumer sends an acknowledgement (ack), and the queue finally deletes it.
The queue hands order 2 to the free consumer.
Disaster: the consumer crashes mid-cook, before sending any ack.
No ack arrives, so the queue keeps order 2 instead of deleting it. It will retry.
The consumer restarts and the queue redelivers order 2. Nothing was lost.
This time the ack arrives and order 2 is removed. Order 3 is next. Retry plus ack means at-least-once delivery.
